summary_zh: 东京都写真美术馆展览《恵比寿映像祭2027（仮）》，展期 2027-02-05 至 2027-02-21。展期取自场馆官网；票价、休馆日与预约以原文为准。

article_text:
B1F･2F･3F展示室

恵比寿映像祭2027（仮）

2027.2.5 （金） — 2.21 （日）

開催期間：2027年2月5日（金） ～ 2月21日（日）

休館日：毎週月曜日（月曜日が祝休日の場合は開館し、翌平日休館）

料金：未定

3階展示室のみ3月22日まで 恵比寿映像祭は、2009年の第1回開催以来、年に一度恵比寿の地で、展示、上映、ライヴ・パフォーマンス、トーク・セッションなどを複合的に行う映像とアートの国際フェスティバルです。映像分野における創造活動の活性化と、優れた映像表現やメディアの発展を過去から現在、そして未来へと継承し共有する場となっています。近年では社会共生の取組や、新進作家の発掘・支援、地域とのつながりの強化やワークショップの開催等にも力を入れています。誰もが映像に親しめる恵比寿最大のアートフェスティバルとして充実を図っています。

title_original: Il bestiario emotivo di Alina Zely in mostra allo Studio Giga di Roma
editorial_title_zh: 阿丽娜·泽利的情感动物集在罗马 Studio Giga 空间展出
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在其创作探索中，年轻的白俄罗斯裔艺术家阿丽娜·泽利（Alina Zely）探索了经验与梦想之间的边界：罗马 Studio Giga 空间举办展览“Sensational Zoo”。本文《阿丽娜·泽利的情感动物集在罗马 Studio Giga 空间展出》源自 exibart.com。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "白俄罗斯艺术家阿丽娜·泽利（Alina Zely）生于2002年，其绘画探索穿梭于记忆、自传式经验、梦想与潜意识之间。她的个展“Sensational Zoo”将于10月28日在罗马 Studio GIGA 空间开幕。开幕式定于18点至20点举行，并将呈现一场与阿曼达·M·科恩（Amanda M. Koen）共同创作的表演。", "links": [{"text": "Studio GIGA", "url": "https://www.instagram.com/studio.giga/"}, {"text": "Roma", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/roma/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展出作品构成了一部没有精确时间线索的日记片段，其中生活经历与来自梦境的影像、欲望、恐惧、回忆以及日常生活的暗示交织在一起。在这个经验与想象之间的不稳定空间中，符号成为了潜意识领域的元素浮现于绘画表面的工具之一。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "介于记忆、恐惧与欲望之间的动物集", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "动物在泽利的视觉世界中占据着核心地位。鹿、各种生物和森林风景作为象征性的存在和情感与冲动的隐喻不断重现，唤起了脆弱性、本能、威胁、失落、逃离的渴望以及对自由的追寻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览标题“Sensational Zoo”便源自这种意象：一个情感与自传式的“动物园”，其中人类与动物的形象、幻象与记忆在没有预设层级的情况下共存。艺术家构建的动物集由此变成了一个真实元素与奇幻元素相互重叠的空间，并保持了个人叙事与象征维度之间边界的开放。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Carpet-Alina-Zely-2026.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "阿丽娜·泽利（Alina Zely），《Carpet》，2026年", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "从白俄罗斯的艺术训练到罗马的绘画探索", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿丽娜·泽利2002年出生于明斯克，在白俄罗斯接受了素描与绘画的早期学院派训练，随后于2021年移居罗马。苏维埃传统的学院派严谨性在其具象构建和图像的技术控制中依然清晰可辨，但它正逐步面临张力。技术并未被抛弃，而是被用来表现梦想、荒诞、冲动和情感的不稳定性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术家的白俄罗斯血统也穿梭于这一视觉风景之中，让那些与自由、归属、失落和压抑相关的问题浮现出来，并被置于一个首先具有自传色彩的维度之内。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Alina-Zely-nel-suo-studio-2.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "在工作室中的阿丽娜·泽利", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "与阿曼达·M·科恩（Amanda M. Koen）的表演", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "借着10月28日展览开幕之际，“Sensational Zoo”还将通过阿丽娜·泽利与阿曼达·M·科恩的一场介入创作，延伸至表演维度。这场表演将围绕一场交换展开：泽利将为参观者创作一幅速写肖像，作为回报，参观者则需要在科恩设计的一个祈愿装置上寄存一件个人物品。该物品必须代表参与者现实中的一个重要片段，并且是经过清醒抉择而留在空间中的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "收到的肖像与交出的物品将共同构成“付出以换取回报”（do ut des）的两个部分：一份痕迹将被归还，而另一份则会留在展览内部。这件物品将成为交出它的人的象征替代品，并逐渐将展览空间转变为一个充满交换、存在与失落的场所。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Aprirà il 28 ottobre, allo Studio GIGA di Roma , Sensational Zoo , mostra personale di Alina Zely , artista bielorussa classe 2002 la cui ricerca pittorica si muove tra memoria, esperienza autobiografica, sogno e inconscio. L’opening è in programma dalle 18 alle 20, con una performance realizzata insieme ad Amanda M. Koen .

Le opere in mostra si configurano come frammenti di un diario privo di una scansione cronologica precisa, nel quale episodi vissuti si intrecciano a immagini provenienti dal sogno, desideri, paure, ricordi e suggestioni della quotidianità. In questo spazio instabile tra esperienza e immaginazione, il simbolo diventa uno degli strumenti attraverso cui elementi appartenenti alla sfera inconscia possono emergere sulla superficie pittorica.

Un bestiario tra memoria, paura e desiderio

Gli animali occupano una posizione centrale nell’universo visivo di Zely. Cervi, creature e paesaggi boschivi ricorrono come presenze simboliche e metafore di emozioni e pulsioni, chiamando in causa vulnerabilità, istinto, minaccia, perdita, desiderio di fuga e ricerca della libertà.

Da questo immaginario deriva il titolo Sensational Zoo : uno “zoo” emotivo e autobiografico nel quale figure umane e animali, apparizioni e ricordi convivono senza una gerarchia prestabilita. Il bestiario costruito dall’artista diventa così uno spazio nel quale elementi reali e fantastici si sovrappongono, mantenendo aperto il confine tra narrazione personale e dimensione simbolica.

Dalla formazione bielorussa alla ricerca pittorica a Roma

Nata a Minsk nel 2002, Alina Zely ha ricevuto in Bielorussia una prima formazione accademica nel disegno e nella pittura, prima di trasferirsi a Roma nel 2021. Il rigore della tradizione accademica di matrice sovietica rimane riconoscibile nella costruzione figurativa e nel controllo tecnico delle immagini ma viene progressivamente sottoposto a tensione. La tecnica non viene abbandonata, bensì utilizzata per rappresentare sogno, assurdo, pulsione e instabilità emotiva.

Anche l’origine bielorussa dell’artista attraversa questo paesaggio visivo, facendo emergere questioni legate alla libertà, all’appartenenza, alla perdita e alla costrizione, inserite all’interno di una dimensione che rimane innanzitutto autobiografica.

La performance con Amanda M. Koen

In occasione dell’opening del 28 ottobre, Sensational Zoo si estenderà anche in una dimensione performativa attraverso un intervento di Alina Zely e Amanda M. Koen. La performance sarà costruita intorno a uno scambio: Zely realizzerà un rapido ritratto del visitatore in cambio del deposito di un oggetto personale su un dispositivo votivo ideato da Koen. L’oggetto dovrà rappresentare un frammento significativo della realtà del partecipante, scelto consapevolmente per essere lasciato nello spazio.

Il ritratto ricevuto e l’oggetto ceduto costituiranno così le due parti di un do ut des : una traccia verrà restituita, mentre l’altra rimarrà all’interno della mostra. L’oggetto diventerà il sostituto simbolico della persona che lo ha consegnato, trasformando progressivamente lo spazio espositivo in un luogo di scambio, presenza e perdita.

写真家・七菜乃の個展「unlearn」が、2026年10月20日から11月1日まで東京・銀座のArt Gallery M84で開催される。森や室内を舞台に撮影した最新の集団ヌード作品約20点を通して、身体や裸に無意識のうちに結びつけられてきた意味や固定観念を問い直す。

長年にわたりヌードを撮影し、自らも被写体となってきた七菜乃。人間の裸は誰もが持つ自然な姿である一方、社会のなかでは現在も性的なものとして強く意味づけられていると考え、その見方が本当に「当たり前」なのかを写真によって問い続けてきた。近年、海外で撮影を重ねるなかで関心は裸だけにとどまらず、人や風景、物を問わず、光のなかで心を動かされたものへと広がっているという。

「unlearn」は、そんな七菜乃がしばらく離れていた集団ヌードに再び取り組んだシリーズだ。森を歩き、部屋に立ち、重なり、そして離れていく複数の身体。そこに作家が見いだしたのは、裸であることをことさらに強調するのではなく、「ただ人が共に在る」状態だった。展覧会タイトルの「unlearn＝学びほぐす」という言葉が示唆するように、裸を見ることを入り口として、見る側が自身のなかにある「当たり前」を捉え直すことを促す。

公開された作品では、柔らかくにじむような光のなか、森に集う身体や建築の内部と外部に点在する人々などが捉えられている。裸体そのものを強調するというより、身体が風景や光の一部へ溶け込んでいくようなイメージが印象的だ。

七菜乃は、身体と光の関係を通して、人の存在と共生の美を探ってきた写真家。国内外で作品を発表し、『LONG VACATION』『裸体というドレス』『My Aesthetic Feeling』などの写真集を刊行している。

タイトル

七菜乃写真展「unlearn」

場所

Art Gallery M84（東京都中央区銀座4-11-3 ウインド銀座ビル5階）

会期

2026年10月20日（火）〜11月1日（日）

時間

10:30〜18:30（最終日17:00まで）

休み

無し

料金

500円※成人限定

article_text:
Denis Villeneuve recently told Empire that he returned to “Dune” for a third and final chapter so he can be “severe with the material,” and that his upcoming James Bond movie will be the “very powerful rocket” he needs to “pull me away from Arrakis.”

“I said, ‘Maybe it’s a good idea to go back to this project, not out of nostalgia, not because I miss it, but the opposite — I’m tired of it.’ I want to make sure that I will be severe with the material. That I will not be complacent,” he explained. “I thought, ‘When it’s done, I need a very powerful rocket to pull me away from Arrakis.’ When I was asked to do the next Bond, I said: ‘OK, this is what I need.’”

Related Stories

Agents and Indie Producers Argue Incentives Alone Won't Fix Hollywood's Ills

Agencies and Producers Back U.S. Tax Incentive as 'First Step' Toward Hollywood Recovery

Villeneuve, director of “Prisoners,” “Sicario” and “Arrival,” has not helmed a film outside the “Dune” franchise since “Part One” was released in 2021. “Dune: Part Two” hit theaters in 2024, and “Dune: Part Three” will debut on Dec. 18, 2026.

Popular on Variety

In June 2025, it was revealed that Villeneuve, a self-described “die-hard Bond fan,” will direct the next 007 movie . There’s been much speculation about who will take up the mantle after Daniel Craig’s 15-year run. Gary Oldman recently claimed that the next James Bond has already been picked , but no official casting announcement has been made.

Based on Frank Herbert’s “Dune Messiah,” “Dune: Part Three” chronicles Paul Atreides’ fall from prophetic liberator to tyrannical emperor. Timothée Chalamet stars as Paul alongside Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Florence Pugh, Robert Pattinson, Anya Taylor-Joy, Rebecca Ferguson, Josh Brolin and Javier Bardem.

In her own sit-down with Empire , Zendaya discussed the arc of her character, Chani, in “Dune: Part 3.” She revealed that in the new film, Chani feels “a deep pain” and “a deep betrayal” as Paul becomes unrecognizable from the man she fell in love with.

“In the previous film, she opened herself up to the idea of letting someone in, allowing a space for love or gentleness,” she said. “Well, we see how that goes. That part of her life is not as present anymore.”

title_original: In Brussels, Photographers Set the Sun-Drawing Alight
editorial_title_zh: 在布鲁塞尔，摄影家们点亮“日光画”
editorial_excerpt_zh: 值此摄影术诞生二百周年之际，法国国家造型艺术中心与布鲁塞尔 Hangar 艺术中心联袂呈现了一场雄心勃勃且震撼人心的展览“重塑摄影”：二十位比利时与法国艺术家通过……对这一媒介展开质问、颠覆与复活。

"二百年前，尼谢福尔·涅普斯将一块锡板放在他勃艮第住所的窗前并静静等待。数小时流逝；光线完成了它的工作。没有画笔，没有凿子——只有犹太沥青在阳光下的化学反应，世界在无人协助的情况下，将自身镌刻到了感光表面上。他的同时代人将其称为“日光画”，这种惊叹与七十年后卢米埃尔兄弟的观众观看他们第一场电影放映时如出一辙：一辆火车正驶入拉西奥塔车站。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在人工智能时代，图像依然可以无需相机而诞生。图像哲学家罗兰·巴特所珍视的“曾经存在”，即某种真实事物曾立于镜头之前的确定性，已不再成立。在2026年，面孔、风景和超现实场景凭空被召唤出来。正是在这种巨大的技术震颤中，Cnap 与布鲁塞尔致力于当代摄影的艺术中心 Hangar 委任了二十位艺术家：十五位来自法国，五位来自比利时，皆通过公开征集选出。这既非怀旧，也非仪式性的庆祝，而是一场关于这一媒介未来可能形态的共同实验。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "对起源的回归始于物质。常驻布鲁塞尔的艺术家朱莉·卡尔贝尔收集了模拟摄影的化学残留物，将它们重新引入实验室并使其再度运转。从感光表面中涌现出她称之为“不稳定制图学”的形成、传播与侵蚀现象。图像自行到来，带有某种几乎是有机的自主性：摄影收复了其最初的状态——一个任由其自身的化学反应——而艺术家也收复了她作为引导而不发号施令的见证者的状态。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一些人则向时间臣服。法国摄影师玛丽·博沃在夜间使用大画幅相机进行拍摄，曝光时间长达九小时，仅靠月光与群星照明。她的“许普诺斯之林”系列从坦纳龙的含羞草林一直延伸到阿尔及利亚的蒂帕扎山丘，那里的植被已经覆盖了殖民地时期的穆斯林古墓。夜空中划过卫星的发光轨迹，而树木则承载着数个世纪埋藏的记忆，“唯有通过时间方可察觉的运动之静止凝聚态”。", "translated": true}, "在楼下，视觉艺术家弗朗索瓦·贝拉巴斯的宏大装置如同一座巨石般拔地而起：一个与人体等大的屏幕倾泻出一种抽象而响亮的物质，他的分身胚胎从中浮现、清晰、消解、重生。艺术家用自己的图像喂养了一个算法，然后在形态仍旧抽象、机器尚未完成其发明的那一刻“切断了进程”。“我们的图像变成了机器的燃料，在异质的时间中被计算”：通过拦截这一股洪流，他赋予了其数字分身一个“得以成形的空间”。访客逗留的时间越长，分身就越发凝实。最终反而是观者遭到了凝视。", "同样的张力——在摄影师与其机械分身之间——也存在于塞巴斯蒂安·范·马莱盖姆的作品中。作为一名经验丰富的战地摄影记者，他在北欧从事了十五年的黑白社会纪实实践，此次他通过《V》（2026）转向了彩色，转向了马德拉岛和亚速尔群岛的光线，也转向了机器。他印在钡地纸上的作品与一部完全由人工智能根据其自身照片生成的影片展开了对话。“摄影提供了一个平静与美丽的空间，而它的动画分身却引发了一种弥散的不安，”他指出。这是一种将生命锚定在纸张上、并将焦虑阻挡在外的方式。", article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Two hundred years ago, Nicéphore Niépce set a tin plate before his Burgundian window and waited. Hours passed; light did its work. No brush, no chisel — only the chemical reaction of Judean bitumen under the sun, and the world inscribed itself, unaided, onto a sensitive surface. His contemporaries called it the “sun-drawing,” with the same wonder that would seize, seventy years later, the audiences of the Lumière brothers watching their first cinematic projection: a train pulling into the station at La Ciotat."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In the age of artificial intelligence, images can still be born without a camera. The “this-has-been” so dear to the philosopher of the image Roland Barthes, that certainty that some real thing had once stood before a lens, no longer holds. In 2026, faces, landscapes and hyperrealistic scenes are conjured from nothing. It is within this great technological trembling that the Cnap and the Hangar — a Brussels art centre dedicated to contemporary photography — commissioned twenty artists: fifteen French, five Belgian, selected through an open call. Neither nostalgia nor ritual celebration, but a shared experiment in what the medium might yet become."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/broyer-anne-lise.-une-fenetre-qui-souvrit-comme-une-orange-1024x701.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "“Une fenêtre qui s’ouvrit comme une orange” © Anne-Lise Broyer", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The return to origins begins with matter. Brussels-based artist Julie Calbert recovers the chemical residues of analogue photography, reintroduces them into the laboratory and sets them back in motion. From the photosensitive surface emerge phenomena of formation, propagation and erosion that she calls “unstable cartographies.” The image arrives on its own, with an almost organic autonomy: photography reclaims its original condition — a chemical reaction left to itself — and the artist reclaims hers, as a witness who guides without commanding."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Others surrender to time. article_text:
Two hundred years ago, Nicéphore Niépce set a tin plate before his Burgundian window and waited. Hours passed; light did its work. No brush, no chisel — only the chemical reaction of Judean bitumen under the sun, and the world inscribed itself, unaided, onto a sensitive surface. His contemporaries called it the “sun-drawing,” with the same wonder that would seize, seventy years later, the audiences of the Lumière brothers watching their first cinematic projection: a train pulling into the station at La Ciotat.

In the age of artificial intelligence, images can still be born without a camera. The “this-has-been” so dear to the philosopher of the image Roland Barthes, that certainty that some real thing had once stood before a lens, no longer holds. In 2026, faces, landscapes and hyperrealistic scenes are conjured from nothing. It is within this great technological trembling that the Cnap and the Hangar — a Brussels art centre dedicated to contemporary photography — commissioned twenty artists: fifteen French, five Belgian, selected through an open call. Neither nostalgia nor ritual celebration, but a shared experiment in what the medium might yet become.

The return to origins begins with matter. Brussels-based artist Julie Calbert recovers the chemical residues of analogue photography, reintroduces them into the laboratory and sets them back in motion. From the photosensitive surface emerge phenomena of formation, propagation and erosion that she calls “unstable cartographies.” The image arrives on its own, with an almost organic autonomy: photography reclaims its original condition — a chemical reaction left to itself — and the artist reclaims hers, as a witness who guides without commanding.

Others surrender to time. French photographer Marie Bovo shoots at night, on a large-format camera, with exposures lasting up to nine hours, lit by nothing but the moon and the stars. Her “Forêts d’Hypnos” series stretch from the mimosa groves of the Tanneron to the hills of Tipaza, in Algeria, where vegetation has overgrown ancient Muslim graves from the colonial era. The night sky is streaked by the luminous trails of satellites while the trees hold centuries of buried memory, “immobile condensations of movements perceptible only through duration.”

More radical still: the renunciation of the gesture itself. In a valley of the Haute Maurienne, in the Alps, photographer and documentary filmmaker Michel Slomka scatters a constellation of camera traps and surrenders the shutter to the forest, the wind, the seasons, the passage of wolves. These devices, he notes, are “less surveillance cameras than small, motionless witnesses.” He has simply “tried to reduce the human footprint to a minimum” so that the animal’s footprint leaves, in the end, a photographic one. The work poses the question: who, exactly, makes the photograph?

It remained to make the dead speak. French artist Stéphanie Solinas unearthed eighteen portraits of young women from the nineteenth century on the American West Coast, driven by a single question: “What do you have to say to me today?” Drawing on a chain of tools running from mediumship to artificial intelligence, the installation “Une sorte de bordel” (2026), on the second floor of the Hangar, conjures from these pioneers a contemporary and animated lineage. A table called “diseuse” — fortune-teller — fitted with a tactile silicone hand, invites the visitor somewhere between oracle and dating app. Algorithms have replaced the ouija board.

On the floor below, the spectacular installation by visual artist François Bellabas rises like a monolith: a body-scale screen pours out an abstract, sonorous matter from which an embryo of his double surfaces, sharpens, dissolves, is reborn. The artist fed an algorithm on his own images, then “cut the process” at the moment when forms are still abstract, before the machine could complete its invention. “Our images, turned into fuel for machines, are computed in alien times”: by intercepting that stream, he grants his digital double “a space in which to take form.” The longer the visitor lingers, the more the double solidifies. It is the viewer who ends up being watched.

The same tension — between the photographer and his machinic double — inhabits the work of Sébastien Van Malleghem. A seasoned photojournalist with fifteen years of social documentary practice in black and white across northern Europe, he pivots with “V”(2026) toward colour, toward the light of Madeira and the Azores, and toward the machine. His prints on baryta paper hang in dialogue with a film generated entirely by AI from his own photographs. “Where photography offers a space of calm and beauty, its animated double provokes a diffuse unease,” he notes. A way of anchoring the living in paper, and holding anxiety at arm’s length.

Laurent Millet, meanwhile, seeks weight in the places where photography resists. “I nearly gave up photography several times because of its thinness, which I could find unbearable,” he confides. His theatres of illusion and scale models, built from nineteenth-century techniques now accessible to all, set a sculptural density against the medium’s transparency. The more objective an image becomes, he argues, the more it operates as a window that erases itself: he demands that it be “something very present, concrete, that pushes back against the eye.”

“To speak of the Bicentenary,” says Delphine Dumont, director of the Hangar, “is necessarily to interrogate the time in which we find ourselves.” The time of history, of creation, of institutions? Perhaps above all, she suggests, “the time proper to art: a time that escapes calendars, but leaves traces.” The poet Théophile Gautier wrote as much in 1864, in a phrase the exhibition catalogue exhumes as its epigraph: “The sun is tireless and photographers will not succeed in exhausting its patience.” Two hundred years after the Point de vue du Gras , other suns are rising over Brussels.

“Reinventing Photography” is on view at the Hangar, Brussels , until 20 December 2026.

The Hangar publishes 200 Years Later: Photography Reinvented by Five Belgian Artists , a leporello devoted to the five Belgian artists in the exhibition — Hangar Edition (2026) . The CNAP and Éditions Poursuite (Arles) co-publish Réinventer la photographie , a book bringing together invited texts and an essay by Jean-Christophe Bailly on the fifteen French artists exhibited (2026) .

(2015)"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Imagining what might have been if Tim Burton’s Superman Lives had got off the ground, documentary maker Jon Schnepp cosies up on screen with his interviewees and insinuates himself unforgivably into the story. The material is almost good enough to transcend his vanity: there is test footage of lead actor Nicolas Cage in his Man of Steel duds, plus interviews with Burton, original screenwriter Kevin Smith and producer Jon Peters, who was adamant that Superman should fight polar bears and a giant spider."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "18. Becoming Bulletproof (2014)"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A group of actors with disabilities form the bulk of the cast of the short western Bulletproof, shot in the California desert courtesy of the inclusive arts project Zeno Mountain Farm. Crucially, Bulletproof itself isn’t about disability, but rather an attempt to highlight the lack of on-screen representation – and plug the gap. article_text:
20. Document of the Dead (1985)

Behind-the-scenes footage from Dawn of the Dead is the highlight of this aficionados-only affair, which follows the 1979 satirical zombie horror all the way through to distribution. Director George A Romero, makeup maestro Tom Savini and the occasional zombie actor shoot the breeze in the deserted shopping mall that provides the movie with its incongruous central location.

19. The Death of “Superman Lives”: What Happened? (2015)

Imagining what might have been if Tim Burton’s Superman Lives had got off the ground, documentary maker Jon Schnepp cosies up on screen with his interviewees and insinuates himself unforgivably into the story. The material is almost good enough to transcend his vanity: there is test footage of lead actor Nicolas Cage in his Man of Steel duds, plus interviews with Burton, original screenwriter Kevin Smith and producer Jon Peters, who was adamant that Superman should fight polar bears and a giant spider.

18. Becoming Bulletproof (2014)

A group of actors with disabilities form the bulk of the cast of the short western Bulletproof, shot in the California desert courtesy of the inclusive arts project Zeno Mountain Farm. Crucially, Bulletproof itself isn’t about disability, but rather an attempt to highlight the lack of on-screen representation – and plug the gap. This affectionate documentary tracks the film from preproduction to premiere.

17. They’ll Love Me When I’m Dead (2018)

Orson Welles spent five years shooting what became his final film, The Other Side of the Wind, with three years elapsing before its star – director and sometime actor John Huston – even stepped in front of the camera. After all that, the footage ended up impounded by the Iranian revolutionary government. A version eventually premiered in 2018 and is now on Netflix, along with this scattershot documentary, presented by Alan Cumming, which strings together archive footage, new interviews and typically Wellesian stories of on-set bluffs, tomfoolery and procrastination.

16. Filmmaker: A Diary by George Lucas (1968)

A half-hour snapshot by Lucas of his new buddy Francis Ford Coppola, who is hard at work on his fourth film, The Rain People, and not too shy to argue with his lead actor, Shirley Knight. Contains one choice detail: in preparation for driving across the country shooting this road movie, all the men on the crew, Coppola included, shave off their beards to look more presentable for any hippy-hating officials they might encounter along the way.

15. Boorman and the Devil (2025)

In declining The Exorcist but taking on Exorcist II: The Heretic, John Boorman perhaps displayed a preference for poisoned chalices over champagne flutes. He is candid and good-humoured, if still a little shell-shocked, as he recounts the experience of filming the sequel once derided as “the stupidest major movie ever made”, and the despair that led him to contemplate self-immolation on Hollywood Boulevard. Sand-related illness, a sozzled Richard Burton, locusts and tap-dancing: this has it all.

14. Doomed! The Untold Story of Roger Corman’s The Fantastic Four (2015)

Filmed in a rat-infested studio on sets recycled from the Jurassic Park rip-off Carnosaur, with special effects entrusted to a local outfit called Mr Film, this cheapo superhero adventure was made in a rush to prevent the rights to The Fantastic Four reverting from producer Bernd Eichinger to Marvel. (“That movie was never supposed to be shown to anybody,” said Stan Lee.) This heartening documentary, which shows the crestfallen cast refusing to let their film die, feels even more pertinent after Warner Bros recently shelved some movies as tax write-offs, including Batgirl and Coyote Vs Acme, the latter rescued only by the skin of its teeth.

13. Jodorowsky’s Dune (2013)

In trying to adapt Frank Herbert’s Dune in the mid-1970s, cinematic shaman Alejandro Jodorowsky (Santa Sangre, El Topo) bit off more than he could chew, just as David Lynch would when his version came to painful fruition in 1984. But Frank Pavich’s documentary proves that Jodorowsky’s intention to make “a film that gives LSD hallucinations without taking LSD” was not too fanciful. Among those in his corner were the artist HR Giger, who went on to design the monsters in Alien, and a cast including Salvador Dalí, Mick Jagger and Orson Welles, with the latter being bribed to take part with the promise of having his favourite chef on set.

12. Lost Soul: The Doomed Journey of Richard Stanley’s Island of Dr Moreau (2014)

When the studio New Line tried to ditch South African director Richard Stanley from his own HG Wells adaptation, he asked a warlock called Skip to pull some cosmic strings. That did the trick for a while, helping Stanley to charm the film’s star, Marlon Brando. But black magic was no match for cast member Val Kilmer, who demanded a 40% reduction in his own shooting days, then spent his time on set playing power games. There was nature to contend with, too, in the form of wild animals (a puma pisses on Stanley’s tailored suit) and a hurricane that ravages the location in Cairns, Queensland. Finally replaced by curmudgeonly veteran John Frankenheimer, Stanley refuses to leave Australia, which is when things go from mad to worse.

11. No Frank in Lumberton (1988) / Blue Velvet Revisited (2016)

Two behind-the-scenes Blue Velvet documentaries from one director. Peter Braatz was still a film student when David Lynch, with whom he had been corresponding for several years, invited him to Wilmington, North Carolina in 1985 to chart the making of what would become his twisted masterpiece. Braatz marshalled just under an hour of the resulting Super-8 material into his 1988 documentary, which straddled the line between orthodox and experimental. He then reshaped it into a full-on ambient head-trip for the 86-minute 2016 version, which mixes flickering footage and crisp black-and-white photographs with a woozy score and the voices of Lynch, Dennis Hopper and others to form an ethereal audiovisual collage.

10. The Sweatbox (2002)

Disney had high hopes for Kingdom of the Sun, a Prince and the Pauper-style animated musical drama set in the Inca empire. The studio sent Lion King co-director Roger Allers on a research trip to Peru and commissioned a suite of new songs by Sting. But it was back to the drawing board after a calamitous screening of an early rough cut; Allers and Sting were given the heave-ho, and the movie was retooled as the larky comedy The Emperor’s New Groove. Sting’s wife, Trudie Styler, charts every disastrous step in a documentary that Disney has done its darnedest to suppress .

9. From Darkness to Light (2024)

A 10-a-penny title for an account of a once-in-a-lifetime film-making folly: Jerry Lewis’s abandoned, incomplete 1972 Holocaust drama The Day The Clown Cried . Directing himself as a former clown who entertains children in a concentration camp, Lewis made a misguided bid to be taken seriously. “It was bad work,” he admits here. It wasn’t only the dubious material that defeated the former Nutty Professor: unbeknown to him, the option on the script had expired, rendering the entire project illegal. It was his decision, though, to hire a repentant former concentration camp guard as part of the crew. “He was a human being!” Lewis protests.

8. Poultry in Motion: Truth Is Stranger Than Chicken (2008)

Seventy-odd fans of horror exploitation studio Troma worked unpaid on Poultrygeist: Night of the Chicken Dead while living in a deserted church in a rundown corner of Buffalo, New York, with one cold shower between them. Meanwhile, the chicken-themed zombie flick was shot at a nearby abandoned McDonald’s. This documentary captures all the on-set horror, from the sexually disinhibited auditions to the hourly cast-and-crew bust-ups. Actors walk off, burst into tears and throw punches; a zombie extra accidentally sets himself on fire; and bilious co-director and Troma boss Lloyd Kaufman proves both lackadaisical and tyrannical.

7. Shirkers (2018)

When budding film-maker Sandi Tan met the enigmatic Georges Cardona, he cited Fitzcarraldo as his inspiration and claimed to know crew members from Apocalypse Now. Those pictures – famously troubled productions that spawned their own jaw-dropping documentaries – look like red flags considering what came next: Cardona directed Tan’s indie road movie Shirkers, swallowing up $10,000 of her savings when he ran out of money, then vanished with the resulting 70 reels of unprocessed film. She didn’t see the footage until decades later, when those reels were returned to her by Cardona’s widow. Tan’s sobering 2018 documentary attempts to make sense of the betrayal.

6. The Peddler (2010)

“Good film directors will notice many mistakes,” says prolific camcorder auteur and 67-year-old Santa Claus lookalike Daniel Burmeister. “But I like what I do: making hand-crafted films.” In exchange for a month’s food and accommodation, Burmeister sets up shop in a remote Argentinian village to bring the community together by shooting a movie from one of his own scripts. His budget may be nonexistent but his resourcefulness is boundless: in place of a dolly shot, for instance, he sits on a blanket, camera on his shoulder, while being dragged across the floor. This delightful, deeply humanistic portrait of grassroots DIY cinema has all the charm and idiosyncrasies of a Jared Hess comedy.

5. Lost in La Mancha (2002)

Terry Gilliam was happy to have documentary makers Keith Fulton and Louis Pepe on set for The Man Who Killed Don Quixote after being impressed by The Hamster Factor, their behind-the-scenes film on the making of his earlier 12 Monkeys. The anguished result shows exactly why Quixote was abandoned after six days’ shooting in Spain in September 2000. Takes were rendered unusable by the roar of F16s from a nearby Nato base; Jean Rochefort, co-lead opposite Johnny Depp, fell seriously ill; and the equipment was destroyed by a merciless storm. Gilliam’s on-set catchphrase sums it up: “We’re fucked!” (When Quixote was eventually made in 2018, Fulton and Pepe documented that shoot, too, in He Dreams of Giants .)

4. Henri-Georges Clouzot’s Inferno (2009)

The subgenre of documentaries about unfinished films stretches back to the BBC’s 1965 The Epic That Never Was, which investigated Josef von Sternberg’s planned version of I, Claudius starring Charles Laughton and Merle Oberon. But it reached its apotheosis with Henri-Georges Clouzot’s Inferno, Ruxandra Medrea and Serge Bromberg’s ravishing reflection on an early-1960s Proustian psychological drama from the director of Les Diaboliques. Lavishly funded by Columbia, Clouzot’s vision was impossibly ambitious, with three crews and a trippy array of complicated in-camera special effects. The director, who could not be dissuaded from shooting time-consuming test footage, suffered a heart attack three weeks into the 18-week shoot. The fragments of his vision, cherrypicked here from 15 hours of unseen footage, are intoxicating: where else can you see Romy Schneider covered in glitter, cellophane and olive oil?

3. Burden of Dreams (1982)

Deep in the rainforests of South America, Werner Herzog battles mud and misery, along with his leading man Klaus Kinski, to make Fitzcarraldo, about one man’s dream of building an opera house in the Amazon. Les Blank’s documentary, which is arguably more compelling than the movie it’s about, enables us to watch in disbelief as a film about a lunatic mission turns into one itself. Herzog’s initial footage has to be abandoned when the lead actor, Jason Robards, falls ill with amoebic dysentery and co-star Mick Jagger is needed on a world tour. Up and running again, the production is forced to relocate more than 1,000 miles away due to a border war, while Herzog’s plans to move a steamship up a hillside provide a textbook example of madness eclipsing method.

2. American Movie (1999)

Mark Borchardt, a Milwaukee junkyard poet with a mullet and plateglass specs, may be best suited to factory work or serial killing, according to his brother, but he positively glows with a passion for cinema. Lacking the funds to finish his feature debut, he instead tries to complete a short horror film, Coven, undaunted by his inability to pronounce the title. More Wiseau than Welles, he has optimism and indefatigability to burn. Not to mention a crew of colourful collaborators, including his mother, whom he enlists as an extra despite her protestations that she needs to go shopping; his bleary, poodle-haired pal and former acid-head Mike; and the gnarled, trailer-dwelling Uncle Bill, who needs 30 takes to deliver four lines. Director Chris Smith (who later made the priceless Fyre festival documentary ) rightly portrays Mark as one of cinema’s most inspiring heroes – even if he still hasn’t finished his first feature.

1. Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker’s Apocalypse (1991)

Megadoc, the forthcoming behind-the-scenes film about Francis Ford Coppola’s $120m passion project Megalopolis , is directed by Mike Figgis, though earlier Coppola-related documentaries tended to be family affairs. The director’s late wife, Eleanor, was responsible for Making Marie Antoinette, released later this month, about their daughter Sofia’s 2006 historical fantasia. And it was Eleanor, too, who co-directed the extraordinary Hearts of Darkness, which draws on her 60 hours of footage and 40 hours of audio recordings, as well as her own diaries, all from the turbulent 238-day shooting of Apocalypse Now. The film reveals her husband arguing on set with Dennis Hopper, frantically typing new scenes just moments before the cameras roll, and negotiating with Marlon Brando, who has piled on the pounds but neglected to learn his lines. “I’m thinking of shooting myself,” the director confides. “This is one crisis I can’t pull myself out of.”

article_text:
With temperatures dropping and the holiday season right around the corner, streaming boosts are all but guaranteed in November. Netflix is diving head first into the Christmas season with the launch of several original holiday movies, but the streamer is also getting a jump on Oscar season with the launch of international awards season hopefuls such as “Possible Love” and “Gentle Monster.” Netflix will also be the streaming home for Chris Rock’s “Misty Green,” which launched at the Toronto International Film Festival in September to instant Oscar buzz for breakout star Rosalind Eleazar.

“Misty Green” is not the only A24 movie that should attract strong viewership on streaming this month. The Dominic Sessa-starring Anthony Bourdain coming-of-age dramedy “Tony” launches on HBO Max right before Thanksgiving after a sturdy box office run over the summer. Netflix, meanwhile, is offering up Peter Berg’s harrowing and inspirational war drama “The Mosquito Bowl” as its big original offering for Thanksgiving weekend.

Check out a full rundown below of the biggest movies streaming in November.

Tony (Nov. 20 on HBO Max) Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection A24’s Anthony Bourdain biopic “Tony,” starring “The Holdovers” breakout Dominic Sessa as the chef and cultural icon, was a modest summer box office hit with nearly $20 million worldwide. The indie coming-of-age drama now arrives on HBO Max just in time for Thanksgiving. Variety’s review praised Sessa for giving a “movie-star performance” and heralded the movie for having “the enchanted spirit of discovery that recalls ‘Adventureland’ and the films of Richard Linklater.”

Misty Green (Nov. 9 on Netflix) Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection Chris Rock’s latest feature directorial effort “Misty Green” is being rushed to streaming via Netflix after debuting in theaters last month via A24. While the indie studio has an exclusive streaming deal with HBO Max, “Misty Green” is launching on Netflix due to the director’s deep ties with platform. Rosalind Eleazar gives a breakout performance as a struggling, self-sabotaging Hollywood actor who gets one last shot at redemption when a dream audition pops up. Variety’s review hailed Eleazar’s performance as “explosively entertaining and savagely authentic.”

Possible Love (Nov. 6 on Netflix) Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection Lee Chang-dong’s acclaimed drama “Possible Love” won the grand jury prize at the Venice Film Festival and is a leading contender to land an Oscar nomination in the best intentional film category. Starring Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Zo In-sung and Cho Yeo-Jeong, “Possible Love” centers on two couples — one pair is a laid-off worker and his spouse, and the other is a documentary filmmaker and her spouse — whose lives intermix in stirringly powerful ways. Variety’s review praised the movie as a “beautifully mature, quietly colossal relationship drama.”

The Mosquito Bowl (Nov. 25 on Netflix) Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection “Lone Survivor” and “Deepwater Horizon” director Peter Berg helms Netflix’s true story World War II drama about four of America’s top college football stars who set their fame aside to enlist in the Marines following the attack on Pearl Harbor. As they prepare for the brutal invasion of Okinawa, they play in a legendary game featuring some of the greatest players in college football history. Nicholas Galitzine leads the ensemble alongside Bill Skarsgård, Ray Nicholson and Tom Francis.

The Uprising (Nov. 6 on Peacock) Image Credit: ©Focus Features/Courtesy Everett Collection Paul Greengrass’ historical thriller “The Uprising” struggled at the box office earlier this fall but should find renewed interest when it streams on Peacock ahead of the holiday movie season. Set in the aftermath of the Black Plague, when King Richard II was levying brutal taxes on his subjects to fund the Hundred Years’ War, the movie stars Andrew Garfield as the leader of a rebellion against the tyranny of the king.

Heartland (Nov. 13 on Netflix) Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection Jessica Chastain headlines Netflix’s country music thriller “Heartland,” written and directed by Shana Feste. The synopsis reads: “Former country legend, Misty Jones, comes out of seclusion to investigate the disappearance of her missing niece, a rising country musician, and must grapple with her own past and Nashville’s seedy underbelly. Her search uncovers a murky side of Nashville where no one, including Misty, is who they seem.”

Gentle Monster (Nov. 18 on Netflix) Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection Lea Seydoux gives an acclaimed performance in Cannes breakout “Gentle Monster,” which Netflix is hoping to turn into a best actress Oscar contender for the beloved French star. From writer-director Marie Kreutzer, the drama stars Seydoux as a concert pianist who has just moved her family to a country house in hopes of easing the severe burnout of her husband Philip (Laurence Rupp). Before they can settle in, an early morning visit from police upends their lives, leaving Seydoux’s Lucy caught between the man she loves and her fear of what he may have done.

Being Heumann (Nov. 13 on Apple TV) Image Credit: ©Apple TV/Courtesy Everett Collection “Being Heumann” is Sian Heder’s follow-up to 2021’s “CODA,” which became a sensation at Sundance and sold to Apple for $25 million before winning the Oscar for best picture. Her new movie is adapted from Heumann’s memoir and follows the activist as she leads over 100 disabled people in a 28-day protest to encourage the government to enforce the section of the Rehabilitation Act that requires all federal spaces to become accessible.

Madden (Nov. 18 on Prime Video) Image Credit: ©MGM/Courtesy Everett Collection Director David O. Russell‘s sports drama “Madden” stars Nicolas Cage as the legendary American football coach and sports commentator John Madden, who was the head coach of the Oakland Raiders in the 1970s, leading the team to its first Super Bowl victory. He became a mainstay of television football coverage, spending three decades as a color commentator after retiring from coaching in 1979. Russell’s movie captures Madden’s career, friendship with Al Davis (Christian Bale) and his partnership with his wife Virginia (Kathryn Hahn). John Mulaney, Sienna Miller and Shane Gillis round out the cast.

Making Marie Antionette (Nov. 6 on Mubi) Image Credit: ©Sony Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection “Making Marie Antionette” is pulled from 80 hours of behind-the-scenes footage shot by Sofia Coppola’s mother, Eleanor Coppola, during the making of the extravagant 2005 period piece. Sofia Coppola shot her third feature film, starring Kirsten Dunst and Jason Schwartzman, at the Palace of Versailles, securing unprecedented filming permission never before granted to any production. This documentary “explores the craftsmanship behind the film, follows costume designer Milena Canonero at work, and offers a glimpse into what it meant to be a young female director at the time.”

Steps (Nov. 20 on Netflix) Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection Netflix’s big animated movie of the holiday season is the musical “Steps.” Per Netflix: “Tired of living in Cinderella’s shadow, Lilith (Ali Wong) steals the Fairy Godmother (Bette Midler)’s magic wand and hijacks the Royal Ball with her sister Margot (Stephanie Hsu), breaking the Cinderella story as we know it and dooming the kingdom to the tyrannical rule of Priscilla (Nikki Glaser), a villainous schemer who swoops in and snatches the throne. Now, Lilith must team up with Cinderella (Amanda Seyfried) to fight biker trolls, outrun evil henchmen, and escape the Screaming Woods on an epic quest to save the kingdom.”

Avedon (Nov. 11 on Netflix) Ron Howard’s documentary on photographer Richard Avedon arrives on Netflix this month. Per the synopsis: “‘Avedeon’ traces the life and legacy of an artist who used photography to reinvent the world around him. Drawing on unprecedented access to his personal archives—never-before-seen stills, intimate behind-the-lens footage, and new interviews with his closest collaborators—the film explores how his singular eye both reflected and reshaped the visual language of the 20th century, and why even the most iconic image is only half the story.”

Super Troopers 3 (Nov. 5 on Hulu) Image Credit: ©Searchlight Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection The entirety of the Broken Lizard comedy troupe — Jay Chandrasekhar, Kevin Heffernan, Steve Lemme, Paul Soter and Erik Stolhanske — return for the third movie in the cult classic “Super Troopers” franchise. Like previous films in the series, the new entry follows a team of mischievous Vermont state troopers and their prank-loving antics. Brian Cox also returns as Police Captain O’Hagan.

Rob Lowe: The Outsider (Nov. 24 on Netflix) Set to release Nov. 24, “Rob Lowe: The Outsider” traces Lowe’s career from his breakout roles in “The Outsiders” and “St. Elmo’s Fire” to his Emmy-nominated performance on “The West Wing” and how he maintained his Hollywood career. The documentary is directed by Chris Smith (“Tiger King”).

The Magic Faraway Tree (Nov. 27 on HBO Max) Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection Adapted from Enid Blyton’s beloved classic novel, “The Magic Faraway Tree” centers on Polly (Claire Foy), Tim (Andrew Garfield), and their three children as they relocate to the remote English countryside. It’s here where the children discover a magical tree and its extraordinary and eccentric residents and get transported to fantastical lands. Through the joys and challenges of their adventures, the family learns to reconnect for the first time in years.

Way of the Warrior Kid (Nov. 25 on Apple TV) Image Credit: ©Apple TV/Courtesy Everett Collection Chris Pratt teams up with director McG for the Apple original movie “Way of the Warrior Kid.” Per the synopsis: “Middle school has been a nightmare for Marc (Jude Hill), a good kid who’s bullied by his classmates and feels like he’s behind in everything. That changes when his injured Uncle Jake (Chris Pratt), a decorated Navy SEAL, comes to spend the summer and recuperate with Marc and his mom, Sarah (Linda Cardellini). To help Marc defend himself, Jake devises an ambitious program he calls ‘Operation Warrior Kid’ based on his SEAL training. Instead of teaching his nephew how to fight, Jake shows Marc what real courage is, facing down his own demons along the way.”

Ice Cream Man (Nov. 20 on Shudder) Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection Eli Roth’s slasher movie “Ice Cream Man” takes place in an idyllic summer town that descends into madness when an ice cream man serves kids from his truck with horrifying results. The horror movie stars Ari Millen (“Orphan Black”) as the eponymous deliverer of sweet treats. The movie is Roth’s first film under The Horror Section banner following the company’s launch in March 2025.

Couture (Nov. 27 on Hulu) Image Credit: ©Pathe Films/Courtesy Everett Collection In “Couture,” Angelina Jolie plays Maxine, a low-budget horror movie director juggling a film commission from a French luxury fashion house while being a single mother in the midst of a divorce when she receives a devastating breast cancer diagnosis. Writer and director Alice Winocour told Variety she wrote the French and English-language drama with the Oscar-winner in mind: “I needed someone special, someone that would have a special connection with the story. Angelina has a lot in common with the character. She’s also a director and she has been through this — not cancer — but everyone knows her story. So I felt like it’s for her.”

Runner (Nov. 27 on Hulu) Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection Owen Wilson, Alan Ritchson and Rodrigo Santoro star in the action movie “Runner,” which “follows a former soldier who is thrown into a brutal race against time when a critical medical delivery makes him the target of a ruthless cartel. With betrayal closing in from every side, he must survive the chase and deliver his cargo before an innocent child runs out of time.”

Guarding Stars (Nov. 18 on Netflix) Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection “She’s a no-nonsense bodyguard. He’s a charming action star. Protecting him over the holidays is her job. Falling for him? That’s where things get complicated,” reads the Netflix synopsis for “Guarding Stars,” which pairs Leighton Meester and Jared Padalecki in a new spin on Katherine Center’s bestselling novel “The Bodyguard.” Expect a Netflix romance hit.

Obsession (Nov. 17 on Netflix) Image Credit: ©Focus Features/Courtesy Everett Collection Curry Barker’s “Obsession” already dominated the box office with more than $520 million worldwide and was a streaming hit when it debuted on Peacock over the summer. Well, expect the buzz to continue as the horror movie makes its Netflix debut just ahead of Thanksgiving.

The Super Mario Galaxy Movie (Nov. 30 on Netflix) Image Credit: ©Universal/Courtesy Everett Collection “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” was the first billion-dollar grosser of 2026 and should keep family audiences hooked to the television when it arrives on Netflix this month after debuting over the summer on Peacock. Returning cast members include Chris Pratt (Mario), Charlie Day (Luigi), Anya Taylor-Joy (Princess Peach), Jack Black (Bowser) and Keegan-Michael Key (Toad). The sequel features the introductions of Donald Glover as Yoshi, Brie Larson as Rosalina, Glen Powell as Fox McCloud and Benny Safdie as Bowser Junior.

Reminders of Him (Nov. 10 on Netflix) Image Credit: ©Universal/Courtesy Everett Collection Colleen Hoover continued her strong run at the box office earlier this year when the “Reminders of Him” adaptation earned $89 million at the worldwide box office. Maika Monroe headlines the romance drama as an ex-inmate who tries to reconnect with her daughter and falls for the best friend (Tyriq Withers) of her late boyfriend, who died in a car accident that sent her to prison for vehicular manslaughter. Variety’s positive review called it “tastefully understated” and a “pleasingly restrained weeper.” The film arrives on Netflix this month after making its streaming debut on Peacock over the summer.

Bonus: Netflix’s Christmas Movie Season Begins Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection November means the start of Christmas movie season, and Netflix is getting a jump on things with the premiere of three original holiday movies. “The Gospel of Christmas” (Nov. 11) hails from Tyler Perry and follows a preacher and his wife who head to New York City to rebuild a failing church. “A Dog’s Perfect Christmas” (Nov. 4) stars Dennis Quaid and Milo Ventimiglia in the story of a dog who must bring his family of humans together when a medical emergency pulls them a part. Last but not least is “The Christmas Switch” (Nov. 12), a French-language holiday movie about a work-hard-play-hard city girl who swaps lives with her homebody sister.

article_text:
The re-release of Ken Russell ‘s controversial epic “ The Devils ” was initially only supposed to be in theaters for one week. However, Warner Bros. Clockwork , which oversaw the restoration, announced that it will extend its run due to “popular demand.”

The film opened last weekend in 350 locations across North America. It grossed over $1.7 million for a per-screen average of $4,925. That’s a respectable result for a re-release.

Clockwork will continue to monitor ticket sales and will keep it in theaters for as long as it keeps performing, according to an individual with knowledge of its release plans. It will be in 315 locations in its second weekend.

The NC-17 film marks the first time that an uncensored director’s cut is available to audiences everywhere. Clockwork premiered the remastered, unabridged version at Cannes and then rolled the film out at key film festivals such as Il Cinema Ritrovato, Toronto International Film Festival, New York Film Festival, Beyond Fest, BFI London Film Festival, Sitges Film Festival, and Festival Lumière.

“The Devils” stars Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed. Its scabrous look at religion, power, and corruption was considered too hot to handle in 1971 (nuns simulating sexual acts with a massive cross had its detractors). Those pesky censors necessitated certain alterations upon release.

But over the decades, the film’s renown has grown and “The Devils” has been championed by movie lovers, such as Guillermo del Toro. The cut was originally reconstructed in 2004 under the supervision of Russell and the film’s editor Michael Bradsell with the collaboration of Mark Kermode and Paul Joyce. The 4K restoration was completed using the original camera negative at WB Water Tower Color, with audio restoration completed using original composite 35mm mag film at WB Sound.

An international theatrical release will follow. BFI will release the film in the U.K/ and Ireland beginning October 30. Theatrical runs will also extend to Poland (October 23), France (October 28), Australia/New Zealand (October 29), Germany/Austria (October 29), Greece (November 12), the Netherlands (November 12), and other territories.
excerpt_original: Clockwork will keep the restored version of the controversial epic in cinemas beyond its one-week engagement.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 罗马里希特画廊展出皮耶鲁吉奥·安东尼奥奇的作品：一种源于宁静的绘画，光线与内省颠覆了目光。文章《皮耶鲁吉奥·安东尼奥奇以意识所见描绘事物》来自exibart.com。

"本次展览名为“从静止中培育光明”，在罗马里希特画廊展出至2026年11月20日，本文的灵感源自这样一个问题：当我们停下来时会发生什么？在静止中存在一种深刻的含义，这是一个我们所有注意力清晰而完整地指向某些感受的时刻。与其将这种状态视为一种心理上的自我中心主义，不如说它是一种以不同于我们通常思考的方式去了解感受和思想流动的方式。这一切促使我们把“静止”视为一种能够调和对立面的行为，因为在静止中，我们的思维得到休息，而通过培育光明，我们获得了一种罕见的内在清晰度。", "在技术层面，这些作品展现了一种朝两个方向发展的探索，一方面致力于体积构建，另一方面则旨在将色彩、光线以及从蓝色开始的色调渐变所蕴含的空间关系吸收其中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "paragraph", "text": "在Antonucci的探索中，关于当代存在与绘画之间关系的反思既紧迫又深刻，即有必要以一种颠倒的视角来生活，从而摆脱一种惯常的感知和诠释自身存在的模式，以一种不同于平常的视角来观察它。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "事实上，与阿布鲁佐乡村的联系并非通过现场写生来确立，而是经过过滤，超越了日常的常态。画面是正面的，略微倾斜和倾斜的，天空轻盈地吞噬着空间，总体占据作品的四分之三或四分之一，房屋的坡屋顶被简化为基本的几何形状，树冠则一棵一棵地绘制出来，而某些地方的裸露土地则与天空融合，仿佛讲述着一种在混乱的手、眼和心的关系中的内在地理。每一幅风景画唤起一种构图原则，让我们产生一种头晕目眩的感觉，仿佛一切尽收眼底，同时捕捉到每一个元素。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正是这些几乎荒凉和无人居住的作品，唤醒了我们的想象力和渴望，想要从内部去体验它们。绘画邀请我们缩小自己，穿越它们，从而迷失其中，沉浸在它们所蕴藏的温暖之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，对于Antonucci来说，形式的简化并不会抹杀其意义，反而通过回归一种原始的视觉谦逊，可以发现艺术家的内省领域。因此，一片天空成为了一个空间界限，有助于理解我们意识到的事物与我们所忽视的事物，正如标记该空间的火焰般的痕迹可以是流动的思维细丝。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/24-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Sabato-nel-villaggio-24x18cm-olio-su-lino-2024-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "Pierluigi Antonucci 作品", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, Sabato nel villaggio, 24x18cm, 油画于亚麻布, 2024, 由Richter Fine Art, 罗马提供, 摄影: Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种方法让人联想到20世纪30年代英国画家Ben Nicholson的风景画作品，不在于形式和技巧，而在于共同的理解绘画是一种对世界的宁静理解，一种生活体验和知识的源泉。参观画廊环境时，显而易见的风景和基本场景的简单性，与标题的珍贵解读相结合，为我们带来意识流，开启了一段关于绘画图像语义的重要时刻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿布鲁佐的土地不是按照地理地形来识别的，而是作为一张地图，邀请我们环顾四周。因此，放弃了对树、房子、天空、海洋的概念，以一种忽视已知事物的目光重新发现最简单的事物，用新的眼睛和清澈的光。因此，半耕的田野和天空的边缘成为超越土地的感受的隐喻，尽管有明显的物质性，这物质被火加热，刚刚变成灰烬，被灰色的烟雾覆盖。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "alt": "", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, Dove la vita è semplice, 20x30cm, 油画于画布, 2026, 由Richter Fine Art, 罗马提供, 摄影: Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这幅画最引人注目并同时让人喜爱的是其缺乏精确性和其破坏性的新鲜感，这两个元素都赋予了整个展览项目最显著的特征。这些搭配保持粗糙和中断，而色调的并置则产生了最意想不到的组合，如同剥落的痕迹，刚刚溶解成新的和弦。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "画家对乡村生活和缓慢节奏的热爱，以及他至今仍生活在其中，使他能够通过基本的形式，几乎像素描一样，将它描绘得纯净。这是因为安东尼奥努奇理解到，根据他的想法，世界是一个复杂的隐喻，因此必须被简化。因此，他提取出既详细又基本的特征，其中内省和回忆在意识中产生，从意识到主题，而不是相反。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "将感知数据置于首位，使我们能够发现画布上的另一个细节：几乎所有作品在某些地方都有不同的厚度和密度，因为艺术家通过连续的叠加，直到图像浮现，就像一种冥想式的吸收过程，其中绘画成为不同深度状态的穿越，最终某物可以浮现并变得可见。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/23-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-La-materia-ricorda-la-luce-resta-12x16cm-olio-su-lino-montato-su-legno-2026-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "皮耶鲁吉奥·安东尼奥努奇，《物质记得，光留下》，12x16厘米，裱在木板上的亚麻布油画，2026年，Richter Fine Art画廊，罗马，摄影：Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这里，一种纯粹出于意愿的独立研究的价值显现出来，无论是因为它起源于一个乡村地区，人们不可避免地回归到真实和本真的事物，还是因为它走的是与当前常规趋势相反和逆流而行的道路。因此，绘画呈现出明显的风格差异，特别是在某些地方，色调似乎摆脱了画家的控制，仿佛是活的、炽热的丝线，根据自主的联想交织在画布上，有时显得自由。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "相反，在最近的作品中，笔触重新组合，稍微回到诗意的形式轨道上，让一幅经过长期沉思、品味、尝试和重试的画布故事以明亮的清晰度浮现，遵循着艺术家沉默的节奏。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/15-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-La-pazienza-della-terra-20x30cm-olio-su-lino-2026-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "皮耶鲁吉奥·安东尼奥努奇，《大地的耐心》，20x30厘米，亚麻布油画，2026年，Richter Fine Art画廊，罗马，摄影：Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一个将展出作品联系在一起的方面是形式的持续开放性，因此紧贴着想象中的礁石的波浪在无限制地破碎，充满“好水”的云朵拥有轻盈、沉重的轮廓，随着飞行而不断变化，如同不断发展的构图。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/7-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Coltivare-la-luce-da-fermi-Installation-view-Galleria-Richter-Fine-Art-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Rome-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, 《在静止中培育光明》, 展览现场, Richter Fine Art画廊, 由Richter Fine Art提供, 罗马, 摄影：Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些选择揭示了一种对事物本质的奇妙自信，只有通过一种罕见的反思能力，才能看到世界，从而‘在静止中培育光明’。这种看似被动的行为，使Antonucci能够重新找到滋养自己故土的根源，了解阳光的舞蹈，如倾盆而下的喜悦雨滴，最终在眼中获得罕见的光芒，这是由内而外产生的视野，而非外在的、分散的视野。", "translated": true}]

Esiste un senso profondo nel raccoglimento, come momento in cui tutta la nostra concentrazione è indirizzata, in maniera chiara e integra, verso alcune sensazioni. Lungi dal considerare tale condizione come una forma di solipsismo psicologico, si svela piuttosto come un modo per conoscere il flusso di sensazioni e pensieri secondo un punto di vista ulteriore e diverso da quello da cui siamo soliti ragionare. Tutto ciò spinge a considerare “ lo stare fermi” come l’azione capace di conciliare i contrari, in quanto in posizione di quiete la nostra mente riposa, mentre coltivando la luce si acquisisce una rara limpidezza interiore.", "links": [{"text": "Coltivare la luce da fermi", "url": "https://www.galleriarichter.com/single-post/pierluigi-antonucci-coltivare-la-luce-da-fermi"}, {"text": "Roma", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/roma/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/3-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Dove-comincia-ciò-che-non-vedo-40x30cm-olio-su-tela-2026-L’ora-dell’aperitivo-20x30cm-olio-su-lino-2026-Dove-la-vita-è-semplice-20x30cm-olio-su-tela-2026-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, Dove comincia ciò che non vedo, 40x30cm, olio su tela, 2026, L’ora dell’aperitivo, 20x30cm, olio su lino, 2026, Dove la vita è semplice, 20x30cm, olio su tela, 2026, Courtesy Richter Fine Art, Roma, Ph. Credit Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Secondo tale prospettiva, le pitture esposte in questa mostra, possedendo una figurazione del tutto estranea a ogni naturalismo, sono in grado di narrare una particolare dimensione in cui la realtà è posta ed esperita dalla coscienza dell’artista, permettendo di scorgere nei dipinti un senso oltre le semplici costruzioni formali."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Sembra che per Antonucci dipingere gli permetta di rendere visibile una rara inversione interpretativa rispetto a ciò che lo circonda, come se ogni opera fosse l’esatto rovescio della realtà ordinaria. article_text:
La domanda da cui origina questo scritto, dedicato alla mostra di Pierluigi Antonucci , intitolata Coltivare la luce da fermi , in programmazione alla Galleria Richter di Roma fino al 20 novembre 2026, è racchiusa nell’interrogativo: cosa succede quando ci fermiamo? Esiste un senso profondo nel raccoglimento, come momento in cui tutta la nostra concentrazione è indirizzata, in maniera chiara e integra, verso alcune sensazioni. Lungi dal considerare tale condizione come una forma di solipsismo psicologico, si svela piuttosto come un modo per conoscere il flusso di sensazioni e pensieri secondo un punto di vista ulteriore e diverso da quello da cui siamo soliti ragionare. Tutto ciò spinge a considerare “ lo stare fermi” come l’azione capace di conciliare i contrari, in quanto in posizione di quiete la nostra mente riposa, mentre coltivando la luce si acquisisce una rara limpidezza interiore.

Secondo tale prospettiva, le pitture esposte in questa mostra, possedendo una figurazione del tutto estranea a ogni naturalismo, sono in grado di narrare una particolare dimensione in cui la realtà è posta ed esperita dalla coscienza dell’artista, permettendo di scorgere nei dipinti un senso oltre le semplici costruzioni formali.

Sembra che per Antonucci dipingere gli permetta di rendere visibile una rara inversione interpretativa rispetto a ciò che lo circonda, come se ogni opera fosse l’esatto rovescio della realtà ordinaria. Si tratta di un processo di interiorizzazione capace di svelare come la natura, composta di paesaggi, alberi, rocce, fiumi e montagne, sia presagio di un lavoro di scavo e svelamento interiore.

A livello tecnico, quanto esposto rivela una ricerca orientata secondo due direzioni, l’una rivolta alla costruzione volumetrica e l’altra intesa ad assorbire nel colore, nella luce e nelle gradazioni tonali che partono dal blu, tutte le relazioni spaziali.

È rilevabile nella ricerca di Antonucci una riflessione tanto urgente quanto profonda circa il rapporto tra l’esistenza e la pittura di oggi, ovvero la necessità di vivere la propria vita da un punto di vista rovesciato , quindi sottraendosi a una modalità abituale di percepire e interpretare la propria presenza, osservandola così da una prospettiva diversa da quella ordinaria.

Tant’è che il legame con il paesaggio abruzzese, dove l’artista vive, non viene fissato dal vivo, bensì filtrato, trascendendo la consueta normalità. Le vedute sono frontali, leggermente sbilanciate e oblique, il cielo inghiottisce con leggerezza lo spazio e occupa complessivamente i tre quarti o un quarto dell’opera, i tetti a falde delle abitazioni sono semplificati in elementari forme geometriche, le chiome sono disegnate albero per albero, mentre la terra brulla in alcuni punti si amalgama con il cielo, quasi a raccontare una geografia interiore nella caotica relazione tra mano, occhio e cuore. Ogni veduta, evocando un principio compositivo, ci permette di avere l’impressione vertiginosa d’aver tutto sotto gli occhi, cogliendone simultaneamente ogni elemento.

Sono proprio queste opere quasi desertiche e disabitate, a risvegliare tanto l’immaginario quanto il desiderio di viverle dall’interno. Le pitture ci invitano a rimpicciolirci per percorrerle e così perderci, immergendoci nel tepore che custodiscono.

Ne consegue come per Antonucci la semplificazione della forma non sopprima il suo senso, bensì, ritornando a una primordiale umiltà visiva, è possibile scoprire il terreno introspettivo dell’artista. Pertanto, una porzione di cielo diventa un limite spaziale utile a capire ciò di cui si è consapevoli a quanto invece si ignora, così come le tracce fiammeggianti che segnano tale spazio possono essere piccoli filamenti di pensieri che scorrono.

Questo approccio ricorda i lavori dedicati ai paesaggi degli anni Trenta del Novecento del pittore inglese Ben Nicholson , non tanto nella forma e nella tecnica quanto invece nella comune capacità di intendere la pittura come una serena comprensione del mondo, come esperienza di vita vissuta e fonte di conoscenza. Visitando gli ambienti della galleria, emerge come la semplicità immediata delle vedute e delle scene essenziali, accostata alla preziosa lettura dei titoli, ci doni un flusso di coscienza , aprendo una parentesi di rilevanza sulla semantica delle immagini dipinte.

La terra d’Abruzzo non è riconoscibile secondo una topografia geografica, quanto piuttosto come una mappa mentale che ci invita a guardarci attorno. Ne consegue l’abbandono del concetto di albero, casa, cielo, mare per osservare, con uno sguardo che trascura il risaputo e riscopre le cose più semplici con occhi nuovi e carichi di una limpida luce. Sicché, i campi semi-arati e i lembi di cielo diventano metafore di un sentire che supera la terra, pur nell’evidente fisicità di una materia riscaldata dal fuoco, appena ridotto in cenere e velato dal fumo grigio.

Quanto più colpisce e fa allo stesso tempo amare questa pittura, è la mancanza di esattezza e la sua dirompente freschezza, elementi entrambi che donano il carattere più incisivo all’intero progetto espositivo. Gli accostamenti rimangono ruvidi e intercisi, mentre dall’affiancamento dei toni nascono le combinazioni più inattese, come tracce slabbrate, appena dissolte secondo nuovi accordi.

Il pittore, innamorato della vita di provincia e dei suoi ritmi lenti che tutt’oggi vive, la racconta fino a renderla pura attraverso forme essenziali, quasi schematiche. Ciò avviene in quanto Antonucci comprende come, secondo il suo pensiero, il mondo sia una metafora complessa e così necessariamente da semplificare. Perciò estrae le fattezze tanto dettagliate quanto essenziali, in cui introspezione e ricordo si inverano procedendo dalla propria coscienza al motivo e mai l’inverso.

Dare la massima importanza al dato percettivo ci conduce a scoprire un ulteriore particolare nelle tele: quasi tutte le opere presentano, in alcuni punti, spessori e densità differenti, in quanto l’artista procede per sovrapposizioni successive, fino a lasciare emergere l’immagine, come in un processo di assorbimento meditativo in cui la pittura diventa attraversamento di diversi stati di profondità, dai quali qualcosa può infine affiorare e rendersi visibile.

Ed è proprio qui che si svela il valore di una ricerca autonoma per pura volizione rispetto alle correnti contemporanee, vuoi perché originata in una terra di provincia, laddove si torna inesorabilmente alle cose vere e autentiche, vuoi perché percorre strade alternative e controcorrente rispetto alle consuete tendenze attuali. Tant’è che la pittura presenta diversità stilistiche evidenti, in particolare in alcune punti i toni sembrano sfuggire a un controllo del pittore, come se fossero filamenti vivi e incandescenti che si intrecciano nella tela secondo associazioni autonome, talvolta presentandosi libere.

Diversamente, nelle opere più recenti i passaggi si ricompongono, rientrando di poco nel binario poetico della forma, lasciando emergere, con splendente chiarezza la storia di una tela lungamente meditata, assaporata, provata e riprovata secondo i silenziosi ritmi dell’artista.

Un ulteriore aspetto che accomuna i lavori in mostra è la costante apertura della forma, così le onde spumeggianti a ridosso di uno scoglio immaginario si infrangono senza limiti, le nuvole cariche di “acqua bona” possiedono profili lievi, pesanti, che mutano volando come composizioni in divenire.

Ecco che queste scelte rivelano piuttosto una meravigliosa sicurezza nel vedere le cose come sono e soltanto attraverso una rara capacità di riflessione con cui guardare il mondo è possibile Coltivare la luce da fermi . Questa azione solo apparentemente passiva, consente ad Antonucci di ritrovare le radici che alimentano il terreno della propria terra d’origine, conoscere la danza dei raggi solari, che cadono come una pioggia battente e gioiosa, sino a ricevere una rara luce negli occhi, sintomo di una visione generata dall’interno piuttosto che dall’esterno diffuso e dispersivo.

Credit Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些作品几乎是荒野的,是无家可归的,唤醒了想象力,也唤醒了从里面生活的愿望,绘画邀请我们重新走路,从而失去我们,沉浸在他们保留的阴影中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此,正如安东努奇所说的那样,形状的简化并没有消除它的意义,而是,回到一个初始的视觉谦虚,可以发现艺术家的无视地面,因此,天空的一部分成为一个有用的空间界限来理解你意识到什么,而不是忽略,以及标志着这种空间的火焰痕迹,可以是流动的思想的小片子。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/24-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Sabato-nel-villaggio-24x18cm-olio-su-lino-2024-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "Pierluigi Antonucci 作品", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, 村里的星期六, 24x18cm, 线上的油, 2024, Courtesy Richter Fine Art, 罗马, Ph. Credit Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种方法提醒了英国画家本·尼科尔森(Ben Nicholson)1990年代的景观作品,而不是在形式和技术上,而是在共同的能力,以绘画为一个温和的世界理解,作为生活体验和知识来源的理解。对绘画图像的色情性有意义。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿布鲁兹的土地不是根据地理地形可以识别的,而不是作为一个心态地图,邀请我们围绕我们。 它导致了树,房子,天空,海洋观察的概念的放弃,一个忽略的观点,并重新发现最简单的事情,新的眼睛和充满清晰的光线。在一个由火热的物质的显而易见物理性中,它刚刚被灰尘所缩小并被灰尘所流浪。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/14-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Dove-la-vita-è-semplice-20x30cm-olio-su-tela-2026-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, 生活在哪里是简单的, 20x30cm, 油在织物上, 2026, Courtesy Richter Fine Art, 罗马, Ph. Credit Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "它越受影响,并同时使这种绘画爱,那就是缺乏准确性和它的迷人的新鲜度,这两种元素都给了整个展览项目的最细致的性格。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "画家,爱上省份生活和它的缓慢节奏,今天生活,讲述它,直到它通过基本的,几乎有序的形状清洁它。 这是因为安东努奇理解,根据他的观点,世界是一个复杂的形象,因此必然要简化。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "把最大重视视觉数据,使我们在电视上发现另一个特征:几乎所有的作品在某些点上都具有不同的厚度和密度,因为艺术家进行后续的超重,直到让图像出现,就像在冥想吸收过程中,绘画成为各种深度状态的过渡,从那里,某些东西最终可以被转移到显而易见。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/23-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-La-materia-ricorda-la-luce-resta-12x16cm-olio-su-lino-montato-su-legno-2026-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, 物质记得,光留下, 12x16cm, 木材上的线油, 2026, Courtesy Richter Fine Art, 罗马, Ph. Credit Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正是在這裡,一個獨立的探索的價值是由純粹的意志與現代流動,你想為什麼起源在一個省份的土地,在那裡你不斷回到真實和真實的事情,你想為什麼走的替代和矛盾的道路與常見的現在的趨勢。他们以独立的组织为主,有时自由地表现出来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不同的是,在最新的作品中,步骤复合,不久回到形状的诗歌二进制中,让一个长久的冥想,蒸发,测试和重复,根据艺术家的沉默的节奏的故事,以辉煌的清晰度出现。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/15-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-La-pazienza-della-terra-20x30cm-olio-su-lino-2026-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, 地球的耐心, 20x30cm, 线上的油, 2026, Courtesy Richter Fine Art, 罗马, Ph. Credit Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一个结合展览作品的方面是形状的不断开放,所以想象的火焰的波浪无限地崩溃,负载“好水”的云层具有轻微的,重的,变动飞行,如组成。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/7-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Coltivare-la-luce-da-fermi-Installation-view-Galleria-Richter-Fine-Art-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Rome-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, 种植灯光, Installation view, 画廊 Richter Fine Art, Courtesy Richter Fine Art, 罗马, Ph. Credit Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此,这些选择在看到事物是相似的更美妙的安全,只有通过一个罕见的思维能力,观察世界是可能的 种植光从停留 . 这种行动只有显而易见的被动,允许安东努奇重新发现的根,营养自己的原来的土地,了解阳光的舞蹈,落下像一个打击和欢乐的雨,直到接收一个罕见的光在眼睛,一个生成的视觉的症状从内部而不是从外部散布和散布。", "translated": true}]

title_original: Elliott Erwitt a Bologna: oltre le immagini iconiche, un racconto intimo e inedito
editorial_title_zh: 埃利奥特·埃尔维特在博洛尼亚：超越标志性影像，一段私密而未曾公开的叙事
editorial_excerpt_zh: 回溯展“埃利奥特·埃尔维特：观察的艺术”（Elliott Erwitt. L’arte di osservare）正在博洛尼亚市立考古博物馆（Museo Civico Archeologico）展出，将持续至2027年2月28日。展览超越了这位摄影师的标志性照片，通过私密领域与集体叙事之间的百幅影像展开讲述。文章 Elliott Erwitt a…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在博洛尼亚市立考古博物馆，观众可以参观展览《埃利奥特·埃尔维特：观察的艺术》，该展由埃利奥特·埃尔维特的长期合作者比巴·贾切蒂（Biba Giacchetti）策展，由Civita文化展览与博物馆公司（Civita Mostre e Musei）与博洛尼亚市立博物馆部门（Settore Musei Civici di Bologna）合作举办。", "links": [{"text": "Museo Civico Archeologico", "url": "https://www.museibologna.it/archeologico/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "策展人本人将此次展览定义为一场“流动的肖像”，而非单纯的回溯展。事实上，从中浮现出的是一位能够游走于公共与私人领域之间、将日常生活与标志20世纪的历史事件交织在一起的艺术家的艺术与人性脉络。正是这种不断转换的记录方式，构成了埃利奥特·埃尔维特绝对的独特性：他有能力展现这一界限是多么脆弱，并通过他的“观察的艺术”加以演绎。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Elliott-Erwitt-4-684x1024.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "埃利奥特·埃尔维特，“博洛尼亚市立博物馆”展览现场视图", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作者的观察艺术显得细腻而从不突兀，它允许观众以静默的方式走入不同的人类处境：从床上小埃伦（Ellen）的肖像，到尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫（Nikita Khrushchev）与理查德·尼克松（Richard Nixon）的历史性会面，再到著名的快照《布拉茨克婚礼》（Matrimonio di Bratsk）。因此，这场回顾展构成了一个连贯且和谐的对话，不同的照片在其中汇聚成一个单一的叙事，证明了重大历史事件与私人时刻是如何由同一条人类的线索紧密相连的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展出的照片中，完美体现这种诗学的是《美国，北卡罗来纳州，隔离饮水机》（USA, North Carolina, Segregated Water Fountains），这张照片成为了20世纪50至60年代美国种族隔离的象征。画面拍摄了一名非洲裔男子正试图从一个破旧的洗手盆中饮水，洗手盆旁边则是一个更为精致的饮水器。墙上那两个具有标志性的词汇——“白人”（white）和“有色人种”（colored）——将这张照片变成了一份见证：人类因偏见而破碎，并成为荒谬社会制约之囚徒的见证。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Elliott-Erwitt-2-684x1024.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "埃利奥特·埃尔维特，“博洛尼亚市立博物馆”展览现场视图", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览包含大约一百幅摄影作品，分为五个部分。奠定这位摄影师国际声誉的影像——从后视镜里的吻到世界政要的照片——与属于他私人收藏的照片并置，其中还引入了一些首次展出的未公开照片。因此，有趣的是，人们所熟知和喜爱的埃利奥特·埃尔维特身边，还并存着其创作中较少为人知的一个维度，展现了他最为私密的一面。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "贯穿并统一整个项目的红线（fil rouge）是他那标志性的讽刺基调。埃尔维特的讽刺以深厚共情的根基为特征，能够将存在的脆弱性、荒谬感以及内在的美感揭示出来。其意图绝非嘲弄，而更倾向于参与：这是一种强调人类共同脆弱的方式，人类在自身不可避免甚至有时颇具趣味的不足中显得无比宏大。他的讽刺与前文提及的公共领域和私人领域的交织相辅相成，弥漫于整个展览：从献给个人影像的板块，到专门探讨讽刺的板块，再到狗的肖像以及作为尾声的自画像系列。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Elliott-Erwitt-3-684x1024.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "埃利奥特·埃尔维特，“博洛尼亚市立博物馆”展览现场视图", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种视觉的源头是一位真正的世界主义者的生平。他出生于法国首都的一个俄国移民家庭，该家庭在革命爆发后不久移居，他在米兰长大，后因种族法的出台被迫逃往美国。尽管度过了基本处于孤独之中的青少年时期，他从未产生过复仇的心态，并与意大利保持着一种特殊的深厚情感——这个他曾多次重返的国家。恰恰是他与意大利的关系构成了展览中备受关注的焦点。这个国家并未被表现为简单的布景背景，而是构筑成一片视觉与情感上的探索和实验领地，正如展览中那些主要拍摄于20世纪50年代的罗马以及该国其他地方的作品所证明的那样。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，这场展览为观众提供了一个深入埃利奥特·埃尔维特艺术与个人世界的私密且崭新的通道。这位摄影师能够以同等敏锐的感知力捕捉事件的戏剧性与日常生活中的讽刺，将直观视觉的即兴性与深刻的概念反思融为一体。正是在这些表面对立却又完美平衡的各要素之间，蕴含着他诗学的本质。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Al Museo Civico Archeologico di Bologna è possibile visitare la mostra Elliott Erwitt. L’arte di osservare, curata da Biba Giacchetti – collaboratrice storica di Elliot Erwitt – prodotta da Civita Mostre e Musei in collaborazione con il Settore Musei Civici di Bologna.", "links": [{"text": "Museo Civico Archeologico", "url": "https://www.museibologna.it/archeologico/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "È la stessa curatrice a definire l’esposizione non come una semplice retrospettiva, bensì come un «ritratto in movimento». Ciò che da essa affiora è, infatti, la delineazione della trama artistica e umana di un autore capace di muoversi tra sfera pubblica e privata, alternando vita quotidiana a episodi che hanno segnato il Novecento. È in questo continuo passaggio di registro che risiede la singolarità assoluta di Elliot Erwitt: la capacità di mostrare quanto sia labile tale confine, declinato attraverso la sua «arte di osservare»."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Elliott-Erwitt-4-684x1024.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "Elliott Erwitt, veduta della mostra al Museo Civico di Bologna", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "L’arte di osservare dell’autore appare come delicata e mai invadente, concede allo spettatore il permesso di accedere in modo silenzioso alle differenti situazioni umane: da ritratto della piccola Ellen sul letto, allo storico incontro tra Nikita Khrushchev and Richard Nixon , fino al famoso scatto Matrimonio di Bratsk . La retrospettiva si configura così come un dialogo coerente e armonioso, nel quale le diverse fotografie confluiscono in un unico racconto, dimostrando come i grandi eventi storici e momenti privati siano indissolubilmente legati dallo stesso filo umano."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Una delle fotografie esposte che incarna perfettamente questa poetica è USA, North Carolina, Segregated Water Fountains , scatto diventato simbolo della segregazione razziale negli Stati Uniti tra gli anni Cinquanta e Sessanta del Novecento. L’immagine ritrae un uomo afroamericano intento a bere da un lavello fatiscente, collocato al fianco di una ben più curata fontanella. Sulla parete, le due diciture emblematiche – white e colored – trasformano la fotografia in una testimonianza di un’umanità frammentata dal pregiudizio e prigioniera di assurdi condizionamenti sociali."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Elliott-Erwitt-2-684x1024.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "Elliott Erwitt, veduta della mostra al Museo Civico di Bologna", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Il percorso espositivo, contenente circa cento scatti, si articola in cinque sezioni. Alle immagini che hanno consacrato la fama internazionale del fotografo – dal bacio nello specchietto retrovisore alle fotografie dei grandi della terra – si affiancano fotografie appartenenti alla sua collezione privata, con l’introduzione di alcuni scatti inediti esposti per la prima volta. È interessante, quindi, come all’Elliott Erwitt più noto e amato si accosti una dimensione meno conosciuta della sua produzione, che ne rivela il lato più intimo."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Il fil rouge che attraversa e unifica l’intero progetto è la sua inconfondibile vena ironica. L’ironia di Erwitt si caratterizza per una profonda matrice empatica, in grado di portare alla luce la fragilità, le assurdità e la bellezza intrinseca dell’esistenza. L’intento non è mai derisorio, quanto piuttosto di partecipazione: un modo per rimarcare la comune vulnerabilità dell’essere umano, magnifico nella propria ineludibile e talvolta persino divertente inadeguatezza.
